solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In France it's good overturning the aristocracy

indicators.note: overturning flips the French word so it reads from right to left

parts.note: the French word for good is bon
still in France, the plural article is les

explanation.surface: A remark that, in France, it is good to topple the aristocracy, a revolutionary sentiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In France' governs both pieces: BON (good) is turned over by 'overturning' to give NOB, then LES is French for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the titled class of a country, its lords and ladies, collectively.

clue.text: Young girls from American city high school entertaining politician

indicators.note: entertaining means taking a guest in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: NY is short for New York
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Pupils at an American high school play host to a visiting politician.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry and myth, nature spirits pictured as beautiful maidens; by extension, any lovely young women.

clue.text: Wild country intimate with weeds

parts.note: a boon companion is a close, intimate friend
docks are broad-leaved weeds

explanation.surface: Remote land where you get close and personal with the weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: BOON is used here in its sense of a boon companion, a close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: American idiom for remote, rough backwoods far from towns.

clue.text: Being ascetic accepting Church initially

indicators.note: accepting means taking something inside

parts.note: the Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of the word Church is used

explanation.surface: Being an ascetic means admitting the church into one's life at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a verb opening the sentence, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one's essence is one's fundamental nature or existence.

clue.text: Food brought back with p-pork in store

indicators.note: in places the stammered pork inside the chewed food

parts.note: cud is food a cow brings back up to chew again
a stammered P before BOAR, a boar being pork on the hoof

explanation.surface: Leftovers returned to the store alongside some pork, delivered with a stammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' suggests a reversal, but cud is literally food brought back up by a ruminant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet with shelves is a place to keep things, a store.

clue.text: Posh toff's valet failing to attend

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
a nob is a toff, a member of the upper classes; the 's is a link
a valet is a manservant

explanation.surface: A grand gentleman's valet neglects his duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Not noticing things, inattentive: attending here means paying heed, not being present.

clue.text: Ship with pirate

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship
and can mean along with

explanation.surface: A sailing vessel together with its buccaneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a bandit or outlaw who robs, as a pirate does at sea.

clue.text: A cry goes up in bowling area

indicators.note: goes up in a down entry means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: to yell is to cry out

explanation.surface: A shout rises at the bowling lanes after a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowling alley is the long lane, or building of lanes, where tenpins or skittles are played.

clue.text: Challenges Egghead missing first answer — one must be up for this competition

definitions.text: one must be up for this competition

indicators.note: missing means a letter is dropped from the challenges

parts.note: dares are challenges

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word answer

parts.note: a sage is a wise person, an egghead

explanation.surface: An intellectual faces challenges without an answer, needing to rise to the contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' means mounted: a rider is up on the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an equestrian contest of precise movements, requiring a rider in the saddle.

clue.text: Wet engaging a left-winger

indicators.note: engaging means holding the A within

parts.note: moist means wet

explanation.surface: A feeble politician charms a radical, wet being slang for weak-willed.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Mao Zedong's communism, a far-left radical.

clue.text: Char speaking with a pleasant manner

indicators.note: speaking says the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: rosily means cheerfully, in a pleasant way

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady talks politely.
explanation.walkthrough: Char is not the cleaner but tea; Rosie Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea, and char is also British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: both clue word and phrase are colloquial British words for a cup of tea.

clue.text: They're after a good time, terribly dishonest

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word dishonest is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Pleasure-seekers described as thoroughly crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure-seekers live for enjoyment, always chasing fun.

clue.text: Girlfriend in just win

parts.note: a squeeze is slang for a girlfriend or partner
at home means in, not out

explanation.surface: A girlfriend, inside, perhaps referring to a lover in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to scrape a narrow victory, winning by the slightest margin.

clue.text: Gulf states first-to-last accommodating British

indicators.note: accommodating means housing another piece inside
first-to-last moves the opening letter of the word to its end

parts.note: says means states

explanation.surface: Persian Gulf states lead a list that takes in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first-to-last' sends the S of SAYS to the end, making AYSS, and B goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a chasm or bottomless pit, a gulf in the sense of a deep divide.

clue.text: End of long race — get tired after Queen gets applauded round

indicators.note: after places the tiring piece behind the rest
round means wrapped around the abbreviation for Queen

parts.note: cheered means applauded
to flag is to tire

explanation.surface: An exhausted marathon finisher is cheered by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The black and white checked banner waved to mark the finish of a motor race.

clue.text: We initial redrafts to prepare for surprise appearance

indicators.note: redrafts says the letters of we initial are rewritten in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone reworks a document they signed to set up a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to lurk hidden, ready to ambush or spring out on someone.

clue.text: Spotted quantity of dry goods in dray

indicators.note: in puts the measure inside the cart

parts.note: a sled is a sledge, and a dray is a low cart or sledge for heavy loads
a peck is a measure of dry goods such as grain

explanation.surface: A measure of grain was seen on a brewer's cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as seen, but it is the adjective meaning dotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: covered in small spots or flecks.

clue.text: Worker after job following surgery

indicators.note: after puts the worker behind the job

parts.note: a post is a job
an operative is a worker

explanation.surface: An employee in search of a position, looking for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes care or the period after an operation.

clue.text: Leftover rum needed by chaps getting tense

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
chaps are men
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Drinking men who need their rum grow anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is not the drink but the old British adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a leftover piece or remnant, such as an odd scrap of fabric.

clue.text: Cons favoured friends

parts.note: in means fashionable, in favour
mates are friends

explanation.surface: Swindles favoured by friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cons' reads as tricks, but it is short for convicts.
explanation.definitionFit: Convicts are prisoners, those held in jail.

clue.text: A guy relaxed

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or rib them

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: comfortable and untroubled, also a soldier's standing-easy order.

clue.text: Cryptically expressed to hoax journalist

parts.note: to cod is British slang for to hoax or kid
ED, an editor

explanation.surface: Speaking in riddles to fool a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Written in cipher, put in a secret or concealed form.

clue.text: You may find some round hot Indian

definitions.text: You may find some round hot Indian

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A note on what you might encounter around a hot-climate Indian.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'You may find' as the definition, which cannot stand for the answer; the whole clue defines it, as the garment is found wound round an Indian.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth wrapped around the waist, worn by men in India's heat.

clue.text: Restaurant egg has peculiar taste about it

indicators.note: about it means the scrambled letters go around the egg
peculiar means the letters of taste are made strange, rearranged

parts.note: egg is old military slang for a bomb or mine

explanation.surface: A diner's egg dish tastes odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' is not food here but old military slang for an explosive device; 'peculiar' makes ESTAT, which 'about it' wraps round the egg.
explanation.definitionFit: French loanword for a small cafe or bar selling food and drink.

clue.text: Witness beauty willing to participate

parts.note: a looker is a good-looking person
on means up for it, as in I'm on

explanation.surface: A spectator, a beauty, is keen to join in.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander or spectator who watches events without taking part.

clue.text: Tramps rejected A levels

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, read backwards

parts.note: tramp and tart are both slang for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: Vagrants turned down for A level exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A levels' reads as British school exams, but A is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Layers, as of rock or of society, stacked at different levels.

clue.text: I sated in chomping small cakes

indicators.note: chomping suggests the letters of I sated in are chewed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fills up by munching little cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicacies, especially dainty little cakes and pastries.

clue.text: Bug broadcasting equipment in extremes of trade

indicators.note: in puts the equipment inside those ends
extremes of takes the first and last letters of trade

parts.note: radio and television sets

explanation.surface: A listening device in electronics shops, bug as spying equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a biting African fly, an insect, here called a bug.
